name: Equatorial Guinea
headline: Equatorial Guinea: −5.8% growth in 2025, 2.3% inflation, debt 35% of GDP
sections: Equatorial Guinea is a $12.8 billion economy (2025), the world's 151st-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew −5.8% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $16K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 22.3% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 2.3% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.9% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 8.3% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 15.7% (2025).
Gross government debt is 35% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 49% in 2020. The general government balance is −0.6% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −2.4% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 75% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 2.3% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 44% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 63.9 years (2024). Population: 1.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
